home.title: Your workspace
home.description: Manage your own endpoints, models and platform access from one place.
home.signedOutBody: Sign in with Discord to see resources owned by your account. The service, not this page, decides access and ownership.

endpoints.title: Endpoint management
endpoints.description: Keep endpoint metadata here; upstream secrets are never returned after submission.
endpoints.baseUrlHint: Enter the full API base URL up to and including the version path (e.g. https://api.example.com/v1). The system appends /models and /chat/completions; do not add those paths yourself.
endpoints.deleteBody: Deleting an endpoint also invalidates its keys, fetched models and bindings. This cannot be undone.
endpoints.invalidUrl: Enter a valid HTTP(S) URL without user information, query parameters or a fragment.
endpoints.noEndpointsBody: Add an endpoint to begin fetching the models available to your keys.
endpoints.secretHint: The key is encrypted by the server and is not shown or copied after this form is submitted.
endpoints.keyHidden: Secret hidden; only metadata is available
endpoints.noKeysBody: Add a key to fetch the upstream model list.
endpoints.modelsEmpty: No models returned for this key
endpoints.modelsEmptyBody: The server returned an empty list. No local placeholder models are shown.
endpoints.similarUrlHint: The server may keep path and slash differences separate; review the canonical URL before saving.
endpoints.keySaved: Key metadata saved. The secret is no longer available in this page.
endpoints.refreshAccepted: Refresh accepted; the server will update the model cache.
endpoints.deleteKeyBody: Deleting this key immediately removes its fetched models and bindings from routing. This cannot be undone.
endpoints.endpointLimit: If the endpoint limit is reached, the server will reject new endpoints without changing existing ones.

models.title: Models and bindings
models.description: Define platform model names and connect them to server-fetched upstream models.
models.providerHint: Provider and model name combine into provider/model, the platform model name seen by callers.
models.modelHint: After creating the model, add a binding that attaches it to an upstream model fetched on an endpoint key before it can be called.
models.noModelsBody: Create a model name before adding bindings.
models.noBindingsBody: This model is a draft until at least one upstream binding is added.
models.deleteBindingBody: The platform model will remain, but this upstream route will no longer be used.
models.invalidOrder: Order must be a non-negative whole number.
models.noEndpointsForBinding: Create and enable an endpoint before adding a binding.
models.deleteModelBody: Deleting a model also deletes its bindings. This cannot be undone.
models.invalidParts: Provider and model are required, must be at most 64 characters, and cannot contain control characters or surrounding whitespace.
models.noEndpointKeys: No enabled endpoint keys are available for binding.
models.noFetchedModels: No fetched models are available for this key.

keys.title: Platform caller key
keys.description: Use this one-time-visible key with the OpenAI-compatible platform exit.
keys.noKeyBody: Generate a caller key only when you are ready to store it in your own password manager or client configuration.
keys.regenerateBody: The current key stops working immediately. The new plaintext is shown once and is cleared when this notice is closed.
keys.oneTimeBody: This is the only time the full caller key is available. It is held in memory only; close this notice after saving it.
keys.copyDone: Copied; close this notice when finished
keys.copyWarning: Clipboard access is an explicit action and is not saved by this page.

issues.title: Issue center
issues.description: Review server-recorded fetch and routing issues without exposing upstream credentials.
issues.emptyBody: The service has not returned any issue records for this account.

account.title: Account and data
account.description: Review account metadata, usage and the two-step data controls.
account.preferencesBody: Your interface language is saved server-side and applies to every device.
account.elevateBody: Export and deletion require a fresh Discord re-authorization. Selecting either action redirects you through authorization and returns you here to continue.
account.elevationUnavailable: The authorization flow could not be started safely. Try again later.
account.elevationRequired: Complete a fresh authorization before using this action.
account.elevatedToken: Elevated token (memory only, if provided by the service)
account.elevatedTokenHint: This value is never placed in a URL, browser storage or query cache.
account.exportBody: The server export contains metadata and usage summaries, never plaintext upstream secrets. The downloaded file is created locally and is not retained by this page.
account.deleteBody: This permanently removes linked endpoints, keys, models, bindings, logs and caller-key metadata after server-side elevation. Type DELETE to continue.
account.deleteWordError: Type DELETE exactly to confirm account deletion.

legal.authoritativeNotice: In the event of any conflict between language versions, the {{locale}} version prevails.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: This policy describes the data used to operate a NonbiriAPI alpha.1 instance.
privacy.notice: Deployment template: before accepting real users, the instance operator must replace the operator identity, contact channel, effective date, retention details and governing-law statements as required by the deployment and applicable law. This text is not legal advice.
privacy.operatorBody: NonbiriAPI is open-source software. Each deployed instance is operated independently by the person or organization that controls that instance. This policy applies to data processed by that operator, not to the public source repository or to Discord and upstream providers acting under their own policies.
privacy.identityBody: The user station uses Discord OAuth for registration and sign-in. The service receives a Discord identifier, username, avatar metadata and the membership information needed for a configured server-and-role registration gate. OAuth access tokens are used during the exchange and are not stored as account data. The service stores bounded account, session and preference metadata. Session cookies are HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite according to the deployment configuration.
privacy.dataBody: The service stores endpoint metadata, canonical upstream URLs, notes, enabled flags, fetched model identifiers, platform model names, routing choices and bindings associated with the owning account. Upstream credentials are encrypted at rest. A caller key is shown once to its owner; the server keeps only an irreversible lookup hash and display fragments.
privacy.credentialsBody: Upstream secrets are never returned in ordinary lists, logs, alerts, errors, exports or URLs. The browser receives key metadata only and does not persist upstream secrets or caller-key plaintext in storage or the query cache. Operators must still protect the server, database backups and master-key file.
privacy.trafficBody: Forwarded requests produce bounded metadata such as account, model, upstream endpoint, timestamps, status, duration and available token usage. Request and response content is not persisted by this application. Bounded diagnostics may contain sanitized upstream context. A reverse proxy or hosting provider may process additional connection metadata according to its own policy.
privacy.sharingBody: When you use the service, request content is sent to the upstream endpoints and providers selected by the account owner. Discord processes OAuth activity under Discord's policies. The instance operator may disclose data when required by law or when necessary to protect the service, users or public safety. Operators must document any other processors, hosting providers or support access they use.
privacy.retentionBody: Request logs are cleaned after up to 30 days. Sessions expire by idle and absolute lifetime rules. Account configurations and usage totals normally remain for the account lifetime; bounded user issues and administrator alerts are limited by caps and state. Account export includes an allowlisted metadata bundle but never plaintext secrets, ciphertext, OAuth tokens, caller-key plaintext or request/response content. Account deletion removes linked account data; operator backups may retain a copy until their own retention cycle and must be covered by the operator's backup policy.
privacy.rightsBody: Subject to applicable law and the instance operator's process, you can update supported account settings, request an export and delete your account through the elevated self-service flow. Deletion is destructive. Contact the instance operator for access, correction, restriction or other privacy requests; the operator must publish the appropriate contact channel before production use.
privacy.securityBody: The service applies ownership checks, encrypted secret storage, outbound SSRF and redirect protections, bounded resources, cancellation propagation and no-store responses to sensitive API operations. No system is completely secure. Do not place secrets in notes, model names, URLs, issue reports or support messages.
privacy.contactBody: The instance operator must publish a privacy contact, effective date and applicable jurisdiction in this page before production use. Material changes to data collection, sharing or retention should be announced and handled according to applicable law.

terms.title: Terms of service
terms.intro: By using a NonbiriAPI instance, you agree to use it lawfully and protect your own credentials.
terms.notice: Deployment template: the instance operator must replace the operator identity, contact channel, effective date, governing law and complaint process before accepting real users. This text is not legal advice.
terms.operatorBody: NonbiriAPI is open-source gateway software, not an AI model provider. The operator of the particular instance controls its access policy, configured upstreams, limits, maintenance and user support. The public source project and its copyright holder do not automatically operate every deployment.
terms.accessBody: An account may require Discord OAuth and membership of a configured server and role. You are responsible for activity performed through your account and must provide information that is accurate enough for the operator's access and support process. The operator may pause new registration or suspend access for security, maintenance, legal compliance or a breach of these terms.
terms.useBody: Use only endpoints, credentials and models that you are authorized to access. Do not use the service for unlawful activity, fraud, abuse, unauthorized access, credential theft, malware, harassment, privacy violations, sexual exploitation of minors, non-consensual intimate imagery, attacks against providers or other users, denial of service, rate-limit bypassing or attempts to defeat ownership and security controls.
terms.upstreamBody: Requests may be processed by upstream API providers selected by the account owner. You are responsible for complying with each provider's terms, usage policies, licensing conditions and content restrictions. The operator does not guarantee that an upstream provider will accept a request, preserve content or keep an account available.
terms.credentialsBody: Keep upstream credentials, caller keys, OAuth links and recovery information confidential. Rotate a credential immediately if it may have been exposed. Do not put secrets in notes, URLs, model names, issue reports or support messages. You are responsible for the content you submit and for having the rights and permissions needed to submit it to the selected upstream provider.
terms.availabilityBody: Requests may be limited, rejected, retried or unavailable because of quotas, ownership checks, safety controls, upstream failures, maintenance or authorization. A successful HTTP response is not a promise that an upstream operation completed unless the protocol response is complete. The operator may change limits or discontinue an alpha service.
terms.dataBody: The privacy policy describes the metadata collected and the available export and deletion controls. Account deletion is destructive and removes linked data after the required elevated confirmation. You remain responsible for independent copies, upstream retention and operator backups that are governed by their respective policies.
terms.suspensionBody: The operator may suspend or terminate access when reasonably necessary to protect the service or users, comply with law or investigate a suspected breach. Where safe and lawful, the operator may provide notice. You may stop using the service and request account deletion through the supported flow.
terms.liabilityBody: To the extent permitted by applicable law, the service is provided on an as-is and as-available basis without a promise of uninterrupted operation, error-free routing, model accuracy, data availability or fitness for a particular purpose. The operator is not responsible for upstream provider decisions or content generated by upstream systems. Nothing in these terms excludes liability that cannot lawfully be excluded.
terms.ipBody: The NonbiriAPI source code is available under the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0. NonbiriAPI, Discord, OpenAI and other names may be trademarks of their respective owners; this project is not automatically affiliated with or endorsed by upstream providers. Rights in submitted or generated content depend on your rights, applicable law and upstream terms.
terms.changesBody: The operator may update these terms for a new release or operational change. Material changes should state an effective date and be communicated as required by applicable law. Continued use after the effective date constitutes acceptance where legally valid; otherwise stop using the service and contact the operator. The operator must publish a contact channel and governing-law statement before production use.
